25:21Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah appeared before one another at Baithsamys, which belongs to Judah.
25:22Judah was routed before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.

25:23Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, at Baithsamys. He brought him into Jerusalem and tore down four hundred cubits of Jerusalem’s wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
25:24He took all the gold and silver, all the articles found in the Lord’s house and with Abdedom, the treasures of the king’s house, and the sons of the mixed company, and returned to Samaria.
25:25Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Joachaz king of Israel.
25:26As for the rest of Amaziah’s acts, first and last, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?
25:27At the time Amaziah departed from the Lord, they formed an attack against him. He fled from Jerusalem to Lachis, but they sent after him to Lachis and put him to death there.
25:28They carried him on horses and buried him with his fathers in David’s city.
26:1All the people of the land took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
26:2He built Ailath; he restored it to Judah after the king fell asleep with his fathers.
26:3Uzziah became king at sixteen years of age, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Chalia from Jerusalem.
26:4He did what was right before the Lord, according to everything his father Amaziah had done.
26:5He sought the Lord in the days of Zacharias, who understood the fear of the Lord. In his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord made him prosper.
26:6He went out and fought the foreigners. He pulled down Geth’s walls, Jabne’s walls, and Azotus’s walls, and built cities of Azotus and among the foreigners.
26:7The Lord strengthened him against the foreigners, against the Arabs living on the rock, and against the Minaeans.
26:8The Minaeans gave gifts to Uzziah, and his name reached as far as Egypt’s entrance, because he grew exceedingly strong.
26:9Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, at the Corner Gate, the Ravine Gate, and at the corners, and grew strong.
26:10He built towers in the wilderness and hewed many cisterns, because he had many herds in Sephela and the plain, and vinedressers in the hill country and Carmel, for he loved farming.
26:11Uzziah had forces that waged war and went out to battle array by number. Their number was recorded by Iiel the scribe and Maasaias the judge under Ananias, the king’s deputy.
26:12The total number of ancestral rulers mighty for war was two thousand six hundred.
26:13With them was a fighting force of three hundred seven thousand five hundred, waging war with mighty strength to help the king against his adversaries.
26:14Uzziah prepared for them, for the whole force, large shields, spears, helmets, breastplates, bows, and slings for stones.

26:15In Jerusalem he made machines devised by a designer to stand on the towers and corners for shooting missiles and large stones. Their construction was heard of far away, for he was wonderfully helped until he grew strong.
26:16But when he grew strong, his heart was lifted up to destruction. He acted unjustly against the Lord his God and entered the Lord’s sanctuary to burn incense on the incense altar.
26:17Azarias the priest entered after him, with eighty priests of the Lord, mighty men.

26:18They stood against King Uzziah and said to him, “Uzziah, burning incense to the Lord belongs to the priests, Aaron’s sons, who are sanctified to burn incense; it does not belong to you. Leave the sanctuary, for you have departed from the Lord. This will bring you no glory from the Lord God.”

26:19Uzziah became angry, holding the censer in his hand to burn incense in the sanctuary. As he raged against the priests, leprosy rose on his forehead before the priests in the Lord’s house, above the incense altar.
26:20The chief priest and the priests turned toward him: there he was, leprous on his forehead. They hurried him from there, and he himself also hurried to leave, because the Lord had rebuked him.

26:21King Uzziah remained leprous until the day of his death. He lived leprous in a house of apphousoth, for he was separated from the Lord’s house. His son Jotham was over his kingdom, judging the people of the land. †
26:22The rest of Uzziah’s acts, first and last, were written by Jessias the prophet.
26:23Uzziah fell asleep with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the kings’ burial, for they said, “He is leprous.” His son Jotham reigned in his place.
27:1Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerousa daughter of Sadok.
27:2He did what was right before the Lord, according to everything his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not enter the Lord’s sanctuary. But the people were still becoming corrupt.
27:3He built the Upper Gate of the Lord’s house and did much building on the wall of Ophla.
27:4He built cities in Judah’s hill country and in the wooded areas, and also dwellings and towers.

27:5He fought the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over him. The sons of Ammon gave him yearly one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. The king of Ammon brought him these each year, in the first, second, and third years.
27:6Jotham grew strong because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.
27:7The rest of Jotham’s acts, his war, and his deeds are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
27:9Jotham fell asleep with his fathers and was buried in David’s city. His son Ahaz reigned in his place.
28:1Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right before the Lord as David his father had done.
28:2He walked according to the ways of Israel’s kings and also made carved images for their idols.
28:3He sacrificed in Gaibenenom and made his children pass through fire, according to the abominations of the nations the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
28:4He burned incense at the high places, on the rooftops, and beneath every leafy tree.

28:5The Lord his God delivered him through the hand of Syria’s king, who struck him, took a great number of captives from them, and brought them to Damascus. He also delivered him into Israel’s king’s hands, and the king struck him a great blow.
28:6Phakee son of Romelia, king of Israel, killed one hundred twenty thousand men mighty in strength in Judah in one day, because they had abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers.
28:7Ezekri, the mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maasaias the king’s son, Esdrikam the ruler of his house, and Elkana, the king’s deputy.
28:8The sons of Israel took captive three hundred thousand of their brethren: women, sons, and daughters. They took many spoils from them and brought the spoils to Samaria.

28:9The Lord’s prophet was there, named Oded. He went out to meet the army coming to Samaria and said to them, “Behold: the wrath of the Lord, the God of your fathers, is upon Judah, and He delivered them into your hands. You killed among them in anger; it has reached the heavens.
28:10Now you say you will possess Judah’s and Jerusalem’s sons as male and female slaves. Behold, am I not with you to bear witness to the Lord your God?
28:11Now hear me: return the captivity you took from your brethren, for the Lord’s furious wrath is upon you.”
28:12Rulers from Ephraim’s sons stood against those returning from the war: Oudia son of Joanos, Barachias son of Mosolamoth, Ezekias son of Sellem, and Amasias son of Chodli.

28:13They said to them, “You must not bring the captivity here to us, for you intend to bring sin against the Lord upon us, adding to our sins and ignorance. Our sin is great, and the Lord’s furious wrath is upon Israel.”
28:14The warriors left the captivity and the spoils before the rulers and the whole assembly.

28:15The men called by name rose and took charge of the captivity. They covered all the naked from the spoils, dressed them, shod them, and provided for them to eat and anoint themselves. They helped every weak person on pack animals and brought them to their brethren at Jericho, the City of Palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
28:16At that time Ahaz sent to the king of Assour to help him,
28:17at this juncture, because Idumeans had attacked, struck Judah, and carried away captives,

28:18and the foreigners had attacked the cities of Judah’s plain and southwest. They captured Baithsamys, Ailon, Gaderoth, Socho and its villages, Thamna and its villages, and Gamzo and its villages, and settled there.
28:19For the Lord humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Judah, because he had utterly departed from the Lord.
28:20Thaglath-phellasar king of Assour came against him and struck him.
28:21Ahaz took what was in the Lord’s house, in the king’s house, and among the rulers, and gave it to Assour’s king, but it brought him no help.
28:22Instead, when he was afflicted, he departed still further from the Lord, and the king said,

28:23“I will seek the gods of Damascus that are striking me.” He said, “The gods of Syria’s king will strengthen them; therefore I will sacrifice to them, and they will support me.” But they became a stumbling block to him and all Israel.
28:24Ahaz removed the articles of the Lord’s house and cut them up. He shut the doors of the Lord’s house and made altars for himself at every corner in Jerusalem.
28:25In every city of Judah he made high places for burning incense to foreign gods, and they provoked the Lord, the God of their fathers.
28:26The rest of his acts and his deeds, first and last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
28:27Ahaz fell asleep with his fathers and was buried in David’s city, for they did not bring him into the tombs of Israel’s kings. His son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
29:1Hezekiah became king at twenty-five years of age, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abba daughter of Zacharias.
29:2He did what was right before the Lord, according to everything David his father had done.
29:3When he was established over his kingdom, in the first month, he opened the doors of the Lord’s house and repaired them.
29:4He brought in the priests and Levites and stationed them on the side toward the east.
29:5He said to them, “Listen, Levites! Now purify yourselves and purify the house of the Lord, the God of your fathers. Cast the uncleanness out of the holy places.
29:6For our fathers departed and did what was evil before the Lord. They abandoned Him, turned their face away from the Lord’s tent, and turned their backs.
29:7They shut the sanctuary’s doors, extinguished the lamps, burned no incense, and brought no burnt offerings in the holy place to Israel’s God.
29:8The Lord became fiercely angry with Judah and Jerusalem and gave them over to terror, disappearance, and hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
29:9Behold, your fathers have been struck by the sword, and your sons, daughters, and wives are captive in a land not their own, as they are even now.
29:10In view of these things, it is now in my heart to establish a covenant of the Lord, the God of Israel, and He will turn His furious wrath away from us.
29:11Now do not slacken, for the Lord has chosen you to stand before Him, to minister and be His ministers and burners of incense.”

29:12The Levites rose: Maath son of Amasi and Joel son of Azarias from Kaath’s sons; Kis son of Abdi and Azarias son of Jallelel from Merari’s sons; Joa son of Zemmath and Jodan son of Joacha from the sons of Gedsoni;
29:13Sambri and Iiel from Elisaphan’s sons; Zacharias and Matthanias from Asaph’s sons;
29:14Iiel and Semei from Heman’s sons; Samaias and Oziel from Jeduthun’s sons.
29:15They gathered their brethren and purified themselves according to the king’s command, through the Lord’s ordinance, to cleanse the Lord’s house.

29:16The priests went inside the Lord’s house to purify it. They cast out all the uncleanness found in the Lord’s house into the courtyard of the Lord’s house, and the Levites received it to cast it outside into the Kedron torrent.

29:17They began purifying on the first day, the new moon of the first month. On the eighth day of the month they entered the Lord’s sanctuary. They purified the Lord’s house in eight days and finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.
29:18They went inside to King Hezekiah and said, “We have purified everything in the Lord’s house: the altar of burnt offering and its articles, and the table of presentation and its articles.
29:19All the articles King Ahaz defiled in his reign through his apostasy we have prepared and purified. Behold, they are before the Lord’s altar.”
29:20King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the city’s rulers, and went up to the Lord’s house.

29:21He brought up seven calves, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for sin, for the kingdom, the holy places, and Israel. He told Aaron’s sons, the priests, to go up onto the Lord’s altar.

29:22They sacrificed the calves, and the priests received the blood and poured it onto the altar. They sacrificed the rams and poured the blood onto the altar. They sacrificed the lambs and poured the blood around the altar.
29:23They brought the male goats for sin before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

29:24The priests sacrificed them and made propitiation with their blood at the altar, and made propitiation for all Israel, because the king had said, “The burnt offering and the offerings for sin are for all Israel.”

29:25He stationed the Levites in the Lord’s house with cymbals, nablas, and kinyras, according to the command of King David, Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet, for the ordinance came by the Lord’s command through the prophets.
29:26The Levites stood with David’s instruments, and the priests with trumpets.

29:27Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. When they began offering the burnt offering, they began singing to the Lord, and the trumpets accompanied the instruments of David king of Israel.
29:28The whole assembly worshiped, the psalm singers sang, and the trumpets sounded until the burnt offering was finished.
29:29When they finished offering, the king and everyone present bent down and worshiped.
29:30King Hezekiah and the rulers told the Levites to hymn the Lord with the words of David and Asaph the prophet. They hymned with rejoicing, fell down, and worshiped.

29:31Hezekiah answered, “Now you have filled your hands for the Lord. Draw near and bring sacrifices and offerings of praise to the Lord’s house.” The assembly brought sacrifices and offerings of praise to the Lord’s house, and everyone eager in heart brought burnt offerings.
29:32The number of burnt offerings the assembly brought was seventy calves, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the Lord.
29:33The consecrated animals were six hundred calves and three thousand sheep.

29:34But the priests were few and could not skin the burnt offering. Their brethren the Levites helped them until the work was completed and the priests were purified, for the Levites purified themselves more eagerly than the priests.
29:35The burnt offering was abundant, with the fat for completing the salvation offering and the libations of the burnt offering. Thus the work in the Lord’s house was set right.
29:36Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because God had prepared for the people, for the matter had happened suddenly.
30:1Hezekiah sent throughout Israel and Judah and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasse, inviting them to come to the Lord’s house in Jerusalem to keep the Passover for the Lord, the God of Israel. †
30:2The king, the rulers, and the whole assembly in Jerusalem took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month.
30:3They could not keep it at that time, because enough priests had not purified themselves and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
30:4The proposal pleased the king and the assembly.

30:5They established a decree for a proclamation to pass throughout Israel, from Beersabee to Dan, inviting people to come and keep the Passover for the Lord, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem, because a multitude had not observed it according to the writing.

30:6The runners went with letters from the king and the rulers throughout Israel and Judah, according to the king’s ordinance: “Sons of Israel, return to the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and He will bring back the survivors left from the hand of Assour’s king.
30:7Do not become like your fathers and your brethren who departed from the Lord, the God of their fathers, so that He delivered them to devastation, as you see.
30:8Now do not harden your necks. Give glory to the Lord God and enter His sanctuary, which He has sanctified for ever. Serve the Lord your God, and He will turn furious wrath away from you.

30:9For when you return to the Lord, your brethren and children shall find compassion before all who took them captive, and He will bring them back to this land. The Lord our God is merciful and compassionate; He will not turn His face from us, if we return to Him.” †
30:10The runners passed from city to city in the hill country of Ephraim and Manasse, as far as Zaboulon, but people treated them with laughter and mockery.
30:11Nevertheless, men from Aser, Manasse, and Zaboulon felt shame and came to Jerusalem.
30:12In Judah the Lord’s hand gave them one heart to come and carry out the king’s and the rulers’ ordinance according to the Lord’s word.
30:13A great people gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very great assembly.
30:14They rose and demolished the altars in Jerusalem. They pulled down everything on which they had burned incense to false gods and threw it into the Kedron torrent.
30:15They sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites felt shame, purified themselves, and brought burnt offerings into the Lord’s house.
30:16They stood at their stations according to their rule, according to the command of Moses the man of God. The priests received the blood from the Levites’ hands.
30:17Because a multitude in the assembly had not been purified, the Levites were responsible for sacrificing the Passover for everyone unable to purify himself for the Lord.

30:18Most of the people from Ephraim, Manasse, Issachar, and Zaboulon had not purified themselves, yet ate the Passover contrary to the writing. Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, “May the good Lord be propitious toward
30:19every heart directed to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, though not according to the purity of the holy places.”
30:20The Lord heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

30:21The sons of Israel present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great rejoicing, hymning the Lord day after day, with the priests and Levites playing instruments for the Lord.

30:22Hezekiah spoke to every heart of the Levites and of those who showed good understanding toward the Lord. They completed the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, sacrificing salvation offerings and giving thanks to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
30:23The assembly together agreed to keep another seven days, and they kept seven days with rejoicing.

30:24Hezekiah contributed to Judah, to the assembly, one thousand calves and seven thousand sheep. The rulers contributed to the people one thousand calves and ten thousand sheep, and the priests’ holy things were abundant.
30:25The whole assembly rejoiced, with the priests, Levites, the whole assembly of Judah, those present from Israel, the resident foreigners who came from Israel’s land, and those living in Judah.
30:26There was great rejoicing in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel, there had been no such festival in Jerusalem.
30:27The Levitical priests rose and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer came to His holy dwelling place, to heaven.

31:1When all these things were finished, all Israel present in Judah’s cities went out. They shattered the pillars, cut down the sacred groves, and demolished the high places and altars throughout Judea and Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasse, to completion. Then all Israel returned, each to his inheritance and their cities.

31:2Hezekiah arranged the divisions of priests and Levites, and each one’s divisions according to his own ministry, priests and Levites for the burnt offering and the sacrifice of salvation, to praise, give thanks, and minister at the gates in the courtyards of the Lord’s house.
31:3The king’s portion from his belongings was for the morning and evening burnt offerings and burnt offerings for Sabbaths, new moons, and the festivals written in the Lord’s law.
31:4He told the people living in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and Levites, so that they could be strong in the ministry of the Lord’s house.
31:5When he commanded the matter, the sons of Israel increased the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, honey, and every crop of the field. They brought all the tithes abundantly—

31:6the sons of Israel and Judah. Those living in Judah’s cities also brought tithes of calves and sheep and tithes of goats, consecrated them to the Lord their God, brought them in, and laid heaps upon heaps.
31:7In the third month the heaps began to be laid, and in the seventh month they were completed.
31:8Hezekiah and the rulers came and saw the heaps. They blessed the Lord and His people Israel.
31:9Hezekiah questioned the priests and Levites about the heaps.

31:10Azarias, the priest who headed Sadok’s house, answered him: “Since the firstfruits began coming into the Lord’s house, we have eaten, drunk, and left a remainder, because the Lord has blessed His people. We have still left this great quantity.”
31:11Hezekiah ordered chambers to be prepared in the Lord’s house, and they prepared them.
31:12They faithfully brought the firstfruits and tithes there. Chonenias the Levite was overseer of them, and his brother Semei was his deputy.

31:13Iiel, Ozazias, Naeth, Asael, Jerimoth, Jozabath, Eliel, Samachia, Maath, Banaias, and his sons were appointed through Chonenias and his brother Semei, as King Hezekiah and Azarias, the leader of the Lord’s house, commanded.
31:14Kore son of Jemna the Levite, gatekeeper toward the east, was over the gifts, to distribute the firstfruits to the Lord and the most holy things
31:15through Odom, Benjamin, Jeshua, Semei, Amarias, and Sechonias, through the priests, faithfully distributing to their brethren by divisions, to great and small alike,
31:16apart from the male offspring from three years old and upward, for everyone entering the Lord’s house for the daily account, for ministry in their appointed divisions.
31:17This was the enrollment of the priests by ancestral houses, and the Levites in their divisions from twenty years old and upward, according to their appointment,
31:18in enrollment with all the offspring of their sons and daughters, for the whole multitude, because in faithfulness they purified the holy place

31:19for Aaron’s sons who served as priests. Those from their cities, men designated by name in every city, distributed a portion to every male among the priests and everyone counted among the Levites.
31:20Hezekiah did this throughout Judah. He did what was good and right before the Lord his God.
31:21In every work he began in service in the Lord’s house, and in the law and ordinances, he sought his God with his whole soul, acted, and prospered.
32:1After these events and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came. He came against Judah, camped against the walled cities, and said he would seize them beforehand.
32:2Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had arrived and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem.
32:3He consulted with his elders and mighty men about blocking the waters of the springs outside the city, and they joined in strengthening him.
32:4He gathered a great crowd and blocked the waters of the springs and the river that divided the city, saying, “Let the king of Assyria not come and find abundant water and gain strength.”
32:5Hezekiah grew strong and built the entire demolished wall and towers, and outside another defensive wall. He strengthened the retaining work of the City of David and prepared many weapons.
32:6He appointed commanders of war over the people, and they gathered to him in the square at the gate of the ravine. He spoke to their hearts, saying,
32:7“Be strong and act courageously. Do not be terrified before the king of Assyria or before the entire nation with him, because more are with us than with him.
32:8With him are arms of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God, to save and to fight our war.” The people took courage from the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

32:9After these things, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians sent his servants against Jerusalem; he himself was at Lachish, with all the army with him. He sent to Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah in Jerusalem, saying,
32:10“Thus says Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: On what have you placed your trust, sitting within the siege in Jerusalem?
32:11Is Hezekiah not deceiving you, to hand you over to death and hunger and thirst, saying, ‘The Lord our God will save us from the hand of the king of Assyria’?
32:12Is this not Hezekiah who removed His altars and His high places and told Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, ‘Before this altar you shall bow down, and upon it you shall burn incense’?
32:13Will you not learn what I and my fathers did to all the peoples of the countries? Were the gods of the nations of the whole earth at all able to save their people from my hand?
32:14Who among all the gods of these nations, whom my fathers destroyed? Were they able to save their people from my hand, that your God will be able to save you from my hand?

32:15Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you or make you confident on these grounds, and do not believe him. The god of any nation and kingdom certainly cannot save his people from my hand and my fathers’ hand; your God certainly will not save you from my hand.”
32:16His servants spoke still more against the Lord God and against Hezekiah His servant.

32:17He wrote a letter to reproach the Lord God of Israel and spoke about Him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the earth did not deliver their peoples from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah certainly will not deliver His people from my hand.”
32:18He shouted in a loud voice in the Judean language to the people of Jerusalem upon the wall, to frighten and bring them down so that they might seize the city beforehand.
32:19He spoke against the God of Jerusalem as also against the gods of the peoples of the earth, works of human hands.
32:20King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about these things and cried out to heaven.

32:21The Lord sent an angel, and he wiped out every mighty warrior, ruler, and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. The king returned to his land with shame of face. He entered the house of his god, and some who had come from his own body struck him down with the sword.
32:22The Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from everyone’s hand, and He gave them rest all around.
32:23Many brought gifts to the Lord at Jerusalem and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and afterward he was highly exalted in the eyes of all the nations.
32:24In those days Hezekiah became ill to the point of death. He prayed to the Lord, and He listened to him and gave him a sign.
32:25Hezekiah did not repay according to the recompense He had given him, but his heart was lifted up. Wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
32:26Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem humbled themselves from the height of his heart, and the Lord’s wrath did not come upon them in Hezekiah’s days.
32:27Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and glory. He made himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, and spices, and armories, and places for desirable articles,
32:28and cities for the produce of grain, oil, and wine, mangers for every animal, and folds for the flocks,
32:29and cities that he built for himself, and a great stock of sheep and cattle, because the Lord gave him exceedingly many possessions.
32:30Hezekiah himself blocked the upper outlet of the water of Gihon and directed the waters downward toward the southwest of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

32:31And so, concerning the ambassadors of the rulers from Babylon sent to him to learn from him about the wonder that had happened upon the land, the Lord left him to test him, to know what was in his heart.
32:32The rest of Hezekiah’s deeds and his mercy are written in the prophecy of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet and in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

32:33Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of David’s sons. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem gave him glory and honor at his death, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
33:1Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
33:2He did what was evil before the Lord, following all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
33:3He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had pulled down, erected pillars for the Baals, made sacred groves, and bowed down to all the army of heaven and served them.
33:4He built altars in the Lord’s house, concerning which the Lord had said, “My name shall be in Jerusalem for ever.”
33:5He built altars for all the army of heaven in the two courtyards of the Lord’s house.

33:6He passed his children through fire in Gai-banai-ennom. He sought omens from utterances, practiced augury and sorcery, and appointed spirit-mediums and enchanters. He multiplied evil before the Lord, provoking Him to anger.

33:7He set the carved object and the cast object, an image he had made, in God’s house, concerning which God had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will set My name for ever.

33:8I will no longer shake Israel’s foot from the land I gave their fathers, if only they take care to do everything I commanded them, according to all the law, ordinances, and judgments through Moses.”
33:9Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, to do evil beyond all the nations the Lord had removed before the sons of Israel.
33:10The Lord spoke against Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen.
33:11The Lord brought against them the commanders of the king of Assyria’s force. They seized Manasseh in bonds, bound him in fetters, and brought him to Babylon.
33:12When he was afflicted, he sought the face of the Lord his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
33:13He prayed to Him, and He listened to him. He heard his cry and restored him to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord Himself is God.

33:14After these things he built a wall outside the City of David, from the southwest opposite Gihon in the winter stream, and where people go out through the surrounding gate, and toward Ophla, and raised it very high. He stationed commanders of the force in all Judah’s walled cities.
33:15He removed the foreign gods and the carved object from the Lord’s house, and all the altars he had built on the mountain of the Lord’s house and in Jerusalem and outside the city.
33:16He set the Lord’s altar right and sacrificed an offering of salvation and praise upon it. He told Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.
33:17Nevertheless the people still worshiped at the high places; yet it was the Lord their God whom they worshiped. †
33:18The remaining deeds of Manasseh, his prayer to God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel—behold, in the accounts

33:19of his prayer, and how He listened to him, and all his sins and rebellions, and the places where he built the high places and set up sacred groves and carved objects before turning back—behold, they are written in the accounts of the seers.
33:20Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the garden of his house. His son Amon reigned in his place.
33:21Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
33:22He did what was evil before the Lord, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon sacrificed to all the idols his father Manasseh had made and served them.
33:23He did not humble himself before the Lord as his father Manasseh had humbled himself, because his son Amon multiplied transgression.
33:24His servants attacked him and struck him in his house.
33:25The people of the land struck down those who had attacked King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
34:1Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
34:2He did what was upright before the Lord and walked in the ways of his father David, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left.

34:3In the eighth year of his reign, while still a boy, he began to seek the Lord, the God of his father David. In the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, sacred groves, and cast objects.

34:4He pulled down before him the altars of the Baals and the high places upon them. He cut down the sacred groves, shattered and pulverized the carved and cast objects, and scattered them over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
34:5He burned priests’ bones upon the altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
34:6And in the cities of Ephraim, Manasseh, Simeon, and Naphtali, and in their surrounding places,
34:7he pulled down the sacred groves and altars, cut the idols into fine pieces, and cut down all the high places throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

34:8In the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Eselias, Maasias the city ruler, and Joah son of Joahaz his recorder to strengthen the house of the Lord his God.

34:9They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the silver brought into God’s house, which the Levites guarding the gate had gathered from Manasseh, Ephraim, the rulers, all the remnant in Israel, the sons of Judah and Benjamin, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
34:10Those appointed in the Lord’s house put it into the hands of the workers, and they gave it to the workers laboring in the Lord’s house, to repair and strengthen the house.
34:11They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy four-foot stones and timber for beams, to roof the buildings the kings of Judah had destroyed. †

34:12The men were faithful in their work. Their overseers were Jeth and Abdias, Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zacharias and Mosollam from the sons of Kohath, appointed to oversee the work; and every Levite skilled in instruments of song
34:13was over the burden-bearers and over all who did the works, task by task. From the Levites came scribes, judges, and gatekeepers.
34:14As they brought out the silver that had been received into the Lord’s house, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the Lord’s law by the hand of Moses. †
34:15Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found a book of law in the Lord’s house.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
34:16Shaphan brought the book to the king and also reported to the king, “All the silver given is in the hands of your servants who are doing the work,
34:17and they melted the silver found in the Lord’s house and gave it into the hands of the overseers and those doing the work.”
34:18Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” Shaphan read it before the king.
34:19When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his garments.
34:20The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Michaias, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaias the king’s servant, saying,

34:21“Go, seek the Lord concerning me and all who are left in Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found. The Lord’s great anger has burned against us because our fathers did not heed the Lord’s words by doing all that is written in this book.”

34:22Hilkiah and those to whom the king had spoken went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Sellem son of Thakouath son of Chelles, herself keeper of the robes. She dwelt in Jerusalem in Masana, and they spoke to her accordingly.
34:23She said to them, “Thus said the Lord God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me,
34:24‘Thus says the Lord: I am bringing evils upon this place—all the words written in the book read before the king of Judah,
34:25because they abandoned Me and burned incense to foreign gods, provoking Me with all the works of their hands. My anger has been kindled in this place and will not be quenched.’
34:26But concerning the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, this is what you shall say to him: ‘Thus says the Lord God of Israel: The words which you have heard—

34:27and your heart felt shame, and you humbled yourself before Me when you heard My words against this place and its inhabitants, and humbled yourself before Me, tore your garments, and wept before Me—I also have heard, says the Lord.

34:28I am adding you to your fathers, and you will be added to your tombs in peace. Your eyes will not see all the evils I am bringing upon this place and its inhabitants.’” They brought word back to the king.
34:29The king sent and gathered the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

34:30The king went up to the Lord’s house with all Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people from great to small. He read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant found in the Lord’s house.

34:31The king stood by the pillar and established a covenant before the Lord: to walk before the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and the whole soul—the words of the covenant written in this book.
34:32He made everyone found in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand. The inhabitants of Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord, the God of their fathers.

34:33Josiah removed all the abominations from all the land belonging to the sons of Israel and made everyone present in Jerusalem and Israel serve the Lord their God throughout his days. He did not turn aside from following the Lord, the God of his fathers.
35:1Josiah observed the Passover to the Lord his God, and they sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
35:2He stationed the priests at their watches and strengthened them for the works of the Lord’s house.

35:3He told the Levites who were mighty in all Israel to consecrate themselves to the Lord, and they placed the holy ark in the house Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. The king said, “You have nothing to lift upon your shoulders. Now therefore minister to the Lord your God and His people Israel,
35:4and prepare yourselves by your ancestral houses and by your courses, according to the writing of David king of Israel and through the hand of his son Solomon,
35:5and stand in the house according to the divisions of your ancestral houses for your brethren, the sons of the people, with a portion of an ancestral house for the Levites,
35:6and sacrifice the Passover and prepare the holy things for your brethren, to act according to the Lord’s word through the hand of Moses.”

35:7Josiah set apart for the sons of the people sheep, lambs, and kids from the offspring of goats, all for the Passover for everyone present, thirty thousand in number, and three thousand calves. These came from the king’s property.

35:8His rulers set apart contributions for the people, priests, and Levites. Hilkiah, Zacharias, and Jiiel, rulers of God’s house, gave to the priests; they gave for the Passover two thousand six hundred sheep, lambs, and kids, and three hundred calves.
35:9Chonenias, Banaias, Samaias, his brother Nathanael, and Asabias, Jiiel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, set apart for the Levites five thousand sheep for the Passover and five hundred calves.
35:10The ministry was set in order. The priests stood at their station and the Levites in their divisions, according to the king’s command.
35:11They sacrificed the Passover, and the priests poured the blood from their hands while the Levites skinned the animals.

35:12They prepared the burnt offering to hand it to them according to the division by ancestral houses of the sons of the people, to bring it to the Lord as written in the Book of Moses; and so until morning.
35:13They roasted the Passover with fire according to the ruling, and boiled the holy things in bronze vessels and cauldrons. It went well, and they ran to all the sons of the people.
35:14After preparing for themselves and the priests—because the priests were offering the fat and burnt offerings until night—the Levites prepared for themselves and for their brethren, Aaron’s sons.

35:15The psalm-singers, Asaph’s sons, were at their station according to the commands of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the king’s prophets, together with the rulers and the gatekeepers at each gate. They did not have to move from the ministry of holy things, because their brethren the Levites prepared for them.
35:16All the Lord’s ministry was set in order and prepared that day, to observe the Passover and bring burnt offerings to the Lord’s altar according to King Josiah’s command.
35:17The sons of Israel who were present observed the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

35:18No Passover like it had occurred in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of Israel’s kings had observed a Passover like the one Josiah observed with the priests, Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to the Lord
35:19in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign.

35:19aKing Josiah burned the spirit-mediums, the spirit-knowers, the tharaphin, the idols, and the karasim that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, to establish the words of the law written in the book Hilkiah the priest had found in the Lord’s house. †
35:19bBefore him there had been no one like him, who turned to the Lord with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength according to all the law of Moses; after him no one like him arose.
35:19cNevertheless the Lord did not turn from the wrath of His great anger, with which the Lord was angry against Judah over all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
35:19dThe Lord said, “I will indeed remove Judah from My presence, just as I removed Israel, and I have rejected the city I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, ‘My name shall be there.’”
35:20Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians at the River Euphrates, and King Josiah went to meet him.

35:21He sent messengers to him, saying, “What is there between me and you, king of Judah? I have not come against you today to make war, and God has told me to hurry. Beware of God, who is with me, lest He destroy you.”
35:22Josiah did not turn his face away from him, but strengthened himself to fight him. He did not listen to Neco’s words through God’s mouth, and came to fight in the plain of Magedon.
35:23The archers shot at King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Bring me out, for I am in great pain.”
35:24His servants brought him out of the chariot, put him into his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried with his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah,
35:25and Jeremiah lamented over Josiah. All the male and female rulers spoke a lament over Josiah to this day. They made it an ordinance for Israel, and it is written among the laments.
35:26Josiah’s deeds and his hope were written in the Lord’s law;
35:27and his deeds, first and last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
36:1The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and installed him as king in his father’s place in Jerusalem.
36:2Joahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem,
36:2aand his mother’s name was Amital, daughter of Jeremiah from Lobena.
36:2bHe did what was evil before the Lord, according to everything his fathers had done.
36:2cPharaoh Neco bound him at Deblatha in the land of Emath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem,
36:3and the king transported him to Egypt and imposed tribute on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.

36:4Pharaoh Neco installed Eliakim son of Josiah as king of Judah in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Pharaoh Neco took his brother Joahaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.

36:4aThey gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh. Then the land began to be taxed to provide the silver at Pharaoh’s command, and each, according to his capacity, exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land to give to Pharaoh Neco.

36:5Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zechora, daughter of Nerias from Rama. He did what was evil before the Lord, according to everything his fathers had done.
36:5aIn his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came into the land, and he served him for three years and then revolted against him.

36:5bThe Lord sent against them the Chaldeans, bands of Syrian raiders, bands of Moabite raiders, and the sons of Ammon and of Samaria. They withdrew after this event, according to the Lord’s word through His servants the prophets.
36:5cNevertheless the Lord’s anger was against Judah, to remove him from His presence because of Manasseh’s sins in everything he had done,
36:5dand because of the innocent blood that Jehoiakim shed, filling Jerusalem with innocent blood; yet the Lord did not wish to destroy them.
36:6Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him, bound him with bronze fetters, and took him away to Babylon.
36:7He carried away part of the vessels of the Lord’s house to Babylon and put them in his temple in Babylon.

36:8The rest of Jehoiakim’s deeds and everything he did—are these not written in the book of the accounts of the days for the kings of Judah? Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers and was buried in Ganoza with his fathers, and his son Jechonias reigned in his place.
36:9Jechonias was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil before the Lord.

36:10At the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him into Babylon with the desirable vessels of the Lord’s house. He made Zedekiah, his father’s brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
36:11Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
36:12He did what was evil before the Lord his God. He felt no shame before Jeremiah the prophet, and at what came from the Lord’s mouth,
36:13in breaking his obligations to King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He hardened his neck and strengthened his heart so as not to return to the Lord God of Israel.
36:14All the distinguished men of Judah, the priests, and the people of the land multiplied breaches of faith in the nations’ abominations and defiled the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
36:15The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
36:16They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

36:17He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.
36:18All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.
36:19He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.
36:20He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
36:21to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.

36:22In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, after the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth had been fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians. He ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom in writing, saying,

36:23“Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has commanded me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea. Who among you is of all His people? His God shall be with him, and let him go up.” †
